Don’t get me wrong chapter 3 was beautifully made and I could see all the hard work poured into it. But they poured that work into parts that I didn’t want. The excess amount of puzzles made me go crazy and while the lore presented was cool, I really had to dig deep into my brain to remember they were there and not just the puzzles. Author: @kelbym3710
Content: In a way it hurts when he leaves, not because he shouldn't have his own life or do what he wants. Often Cory comes back with a promise and an angle from his absences that feel grounding and even inspiring. This time he came back with a comic, showcasing his dreams as well as yours can be achieved with effort and dedication. Even better the message in the comic is about overcoming odds and stepping outside of yourself. However, when he leaves it feels like these words and promises become a memory in a way that are less finite. Will he be back in a week? or literally 9 months? Many times he's talked about improving when he's gone which is such a strong message but it feels strange. Cory is one of the few YouTubers I consistently come back to YouTube to watch, yet I feel lightly attached to staying with the promise he might come back. In a way I wish I could forget the Shogun, just to stop hyping myself up when he returns. I'd never create an insane parasocial relationship with his videos, but every time he comes back he has me craving more like a direction.

Author: @Dial4loveZERI
Content:
It’s been weeks… months, maybe? I’ve lost track of time. My world has slowly descended into a quiet, echoing void since CoryxKenshin posted his last video. The once vibrant realm of "Samurai!" has grown eerily still. My notifications? Crickets. My YouTube homepage? Barren. The search bar? Empty. No new "CoryxKenshin" content. Nothing.

At first, I was optimistic. “He’s probably just taking a break,” I thought. After all, the man had just finished the legendary "poppy playtime" series. I mean, surely, everyone needs a little time to recharge, right? But days turned into weeks. And weeks… turned into months. My optimism morphed into something else—fear. Doubt. A slight addiction to watching old videos on repeat.

I check his channel every morning, like clockwork. "Maybe today’s the day," I whisper to myself, as if my desperate plea could summon him. I tap on his name. A single tear rolls down my face as I see his face staring back at me, frozen in time, forever captured in that last thumbnail. I refresh. Still nothing.

I’ve started setting alarms now—two a day. One at 10 AM, the other at 3 PM, just in case he’s on that "late upload" schedule. “Maybe today’s the day,” I say, again. "Maybe... just maybe..."

I refresh Twitter. He tweets? No. It’s just some random inspirational quote. “But what if… what if he’s tweeting in secret code?” I think. Theories begin to brew in my head. “Could he be stuck in some alternate dimension? Perhaps his gaming setup has taken him to the netherworld, and we won’t see him until 2026?”

I dig deep into the comment sections of his older videos. His fans are like me—absolutely starving for his return. Some are posting memes, others forming support groups. Some have resorted to questionable activities like… starting fan theories on why he’s gone. "The Great Samurai is probably in hiding," one commenter says. "He's secretly training to defeat the ultimate boss level." Another suggests, “What if CoryxKenshin has been abducted by aliens… and they just don’t get the YouTube algorithm?”

I nod, fully invested in this new theory. It all makes sense. Of course, the aliens wouldn’t understand the algorithm! How could they?

My phone buzzes. Could it be… could it be the day? I unlock it, trembling. But no, it’s just another YouTube notification from someone else I barely know. “Welp, back to the drawing board.”

Your impact goes beyond YouTube—your kindness, your authenticity, and your faith inspire so many people. Whatever you decide, we’ll support you, but just know that you are deeply missed. Content:
Legend tells of a great samurai master who would vanish into the misty mountains without warning, leaving his people to wonder if he would ever return. They would whisper, "Has he abandoned us?" but the wisest among them knew better. 

"He is gathering new tales," they would say, "collecting experiences that will enrich our lives when he returns." And so it is with our own Cory. The YouTube dojo stands empty now, the notification bell silent as fallen snow. Some young samurai pace restlessly, their patience wearing thin as paper lanterns. Others meditate, finding strength in memories of past uploads that made their sides ache with laughter or their hearts race with terror. The seasons of content come and go like cherry blossoms,  beautiful in their presence, teaching us appreciation in their absence. When the master returns, he does not apologize for the wait but makes it worthwhile. And when the new video finally appears, like the first ray of sunlight after a storm, the waiting becomes a forgotten dream.  For in the cycle of YouTube, patience is not merely virtuous..it is the way of the true samurai.

Content: This comment is more for me than anyone else. I've been watching Coryxkenshin since 2019, when I was 13. I was in school at the time, at he really brightened up my day. He would always make me smile and laugh whenever something new was posted, and he was a figure I looked up to. But then he started disappearing for months on end, and that really sucked. It felt like I was being abandoned by a long time friend I didn't even know, and it created a really weird dynamic, because every time he would return, it would be great, but only for a while. Overtime, these unannounced breaks really took a toll on my mental health more than I realized, especially this most recent over a year radio silence. Cory, while you might be amazing, funny, and a great YouTube, you're so inconsistent and disregarding of your community. Everyone goes through life, but we tell people we care about, or even give updates. I love the fact that you used your platform to help sell your creative writing, but I think everyone can tell it feels a little off. I've recently graduated high school, and I've been thinking about lot about purpose and who I want to be in life. It pains me to say this, but I don't want to be like you. No notification, nothing when you leave, promoting something then leaving again is wrong. Period. Again, this comment isn't an attack, it's my experience, and maybe it can help others in some way. I know you have 21.3 Million subscribers and you'll never see this, but I'm unsubscribing from "Coryxkenshin" and turning my Spooky scary Sunday (which was also promised but not delivered ) hoodie in to goodwill. You'll always have a place in my mind, but I'm not sure if it's a good one anymore. Good luck, I hope you find happiness, and realize that you're more than just a 9-month return YouTuber. Content:
Opening scene: A bustling hive. Barry B. Benson, a young bee, is graduating.)

BARRY: (Voiceover) According to all known laws of aviation, there is no way a bee should be able to fly. Its wings are too small to get its fat little body off the ground. The bee, of course, flies anyway. Because bees don't care what humans think is impossible.   

(Barry is in his graduation ceremony.)

ANNOUNCER: Graduates of City College, class of 9:15.

(The graduates buzz excitedly.)

BARRY: (Voiceover) Yellow, black. Yellow, black. Yellow, black. Yellow, black... Ooh, black and yellow! Let's shake it up a little.

(Barry and his friend, Adam, are talking.)

ADAM: Barry! Breakfast is ready!

BARRY: Ooming!

(In the kitchen, Barry's parents are waiting.)

DAD: Son, let me give you some advice.

BARRY: No, Dad.

DAD: A lot of jobs out there aren't very glamorous. You know, like picking up pollen, stitching up royal larvae, strapping on high-altitude speed brakes, or…

BARRY: But, Dad, I don't want to do any of those!

MOM: Oh, Barry, just think. Once you pick a job, you'll stay with it for the rest of your life.

BARRY: The whole rest of my life? I'm gonna die doing this job?

DAD: You'll be happy to know that bees, as a species, haven't had one day off in 27 million years.

BARRY: (To Adam) So you'll just work us to death?

ADAM: We'll sure try.

(They enter Honex, the honey-making factory.)

BARRY: Wow! The hive mind is a very powerful thing.

ADAM: Yeah, well, it's got my parents back in B-section.

(A tour guide bee speaks.)

TOUR GUIDE: Welcome to Honex. A division of Honesco and a part of the Hexagon Group.

(The bees are shown various jobs.)

TOUR GUIDE: This is where we make the honey, boys.

BARRY: Isn't that a little dramatic?

TOUR GUIDE: You think this is dramatic? This is where we're going to die!

(Barry and Adam are in the "Pollen Jocks" room.)

BARRY: What is that?

ADAM: That's the pollen tube.

BARRY: Wow.

LOU LO DUVA: You guys ready to rumble?

BARRY & ADAM: Yeah!

LOU LO DUVA: What do you say, newbees?

BARRY: Hey, Lou, you did a lot of buzzing today.

LOU LO DUVA: I'm a little droned.

(The Pollen Jocks fly out of the hive.)

BARRY: (Voiceover) We live on two cups of coffee a day.

(They fly through the city.)

BARRY: They’re our navigators, driving us crazy.

(They land in a flower field.)

BARRY: All right, boys, we’re going to pollinate some flowers.

(Barry flies into a house's open window.)

BARRY: This is insane. What am I doing? Hello?

(He encounters Vanessa, a florist.)

VANESSA: You’re talking.

BARRY: Yeah. I’m talking.

VANESSA: You’re talking!

BARRY: What? You’re freaking me out.

VANESSA: No way!

BARRY: You can talk?

VANESSA: Yeah!

BARRY: You can talk!

VANESSA: What?

BARRY: You can talk!

VANESSA: Oh my gosh!

(They have a conversation.)

VANESSA: So you're a... bee?

BARRY: Yeah.

VANESSA: Wow.

(Barry learns about the human world and the honey industry.)

BARRY: They’re stealing our honey!

(Barry decides to sue the human race.)

(Courtroom scenes ensue, with Barry as his own lawyer.)

BARRY: Ladies and gentlemen of the jury, there's been a terrible crime committed right here in Central Park. Not only has our honey been stolen, but our right to live as free bees has been taken from us!

(Barry wins the case, and honey production stops.)

(The ecosystem collapses without the bees' pollination.)

BARRY: (Voiceover) What have I done?

(Barry and Vanessa fly to get the last of the flowers, and save the world.)

(Barry returns to the hive, a changed bee.)

BARRY: (Voiceover) I learned that even a small bee can make a big difference.

(The end.)

Author: @Pinklemonvr
Content:
Cool here is 2+2

Take a computational approach to the problem. Specifically, consider the encoding of natural numbers in the simply-typed lambda calculus called Church numerals. In this encoding, the number 2 is represented by a function that looks like this:

2 ≡ λf.λx.f (f x)
In other words, the number two is a function that takes a function and some value (let's assume that we're comfortable with currying here), and applies the function twice to the value. In general, a number n is represented by a function that takes a function and some value and applies f to the value n times.

Using the Church encoding, you can define operations on the numbers as well. In this case, you're interested in plus, which takes two numbers and returns a number

plus ≡ λm.λn.λf.λx.???
So what's in the body? Well, the body has to be n + m applications of f to the value x. If we pass f and x to n, we get n applications–call that r, and if we apply m to f and r, that'll be m + n applications of f:

plus ≡ λm.λn.λf.λx.m f (n f x)
So the expression 2 + 2 using this encoding is:

plus 2 2 ≡ (λm.λn.λf.λx.m f (n f x)) (λf.λx.f (f x)) (λf.λx.f (f x))
Now β-reduce until you get the result:

plus 2 2 ≡ (λm.λn.λf.λx.m f (n f x)) (λf.λx.f (f x)) (λf.λx.f (f x))
         ↦ (λn.λf.λx.(λf.λx.f (f x)) f (n f x)) (λf.λx.f (f x))
         ↦ (λf.λx.(λf.λx.f (f x)) f ((λf.λx.f (f x)) f x))
         ↦ (λf.λx.(λx.f (f x)) ((λf.λx.f (f x)) f x))
         ↦ (λf.λx.(λx.f (f x)) ((λx.f (f x)) x))
         ↦ (λf.λx.(λx.f (f x)) (f (f x)))
         ↦ (λf.λx.f (f (f (f x))))
         ≡ 4.
But now, let's bust out of this theoretical prison and say we have a number 0 in some representation that we can actually work with, as well as a function add1 that knows how to increment a number in that representation. Well, then we can get a useable representation out of our church numeral, by applying to the numeral to add1 and the value:

4 add1 0 = 4

Author: @Idekwhyimherengl
Content:
[SPOILERS] So for anyone who's kind of confused on the whole 'A,' 'B,' and 'C' subjects for "project; Doey," I'll explain.


There were 3 boys. Kevin Barnes, a test subject/orphan at playtime Co. Matthew Hallard (Another test subject/orphan at playtime co.) and Jack Ayers (A little boy who got a ticket to playtime co's factory.)

At the beginning, its known that after Jack gets the ticket and goes to the factory, when his parents look away for a few seconds, he falls into the vat of mixing dough and eventually just changes into subject 'C.'

Then from the orphanage, Its known they use kids to make new toys. So originally they chose Kevin to be the child to turn into Doey before Jack fell in because Kevin was fit for it; he passed the mental test, the physical test, etc. But because Kevin was aggressive and got wild when he couldn't hold emotions, they added Matthew, who was known as a sweet young man who would always take care of others, to balance out the emotions between Matthew and Kevin.


But then Jack fell in and sort of messed up the balance. And instead of balancing each other out, it ended up splitting Doey into 3 personalities. So its technically 3 people in Doey: an aggressive boy, a caring, protective teenager, and a little boy who's playful and loves giggling.

Looking carefully at Doey's design, you can see he has 3 hands on his stomach, 1 fiery red for Kevin and his aggressive attitude. 1 bright, soft yellow for Matthew and his caring personality. And one mix of orange to show the young age of Jack and how childish, giggly, and goofy he is/was.


In the green tape after Cory beat the doctor and went back to the Safe Haven, we find out that once Kevin gets overwhelmed, he begins to freak out and get angry, and when he does this, he becomes erratic and aggressive. That's why when everyone died, the part of Doey that Matthew controlled got a little weakened since he felt his job was to protect others and he failed and Kevin was able to overpower it, and since Jack is a little boy with little kid emotions, he didn't know what to do other than cry and whine for his parents.

When Doey is in his final form, he only cries for his parents and yells at 'Player' because Kevin has taken over the Matthew part of Doey that protected everyone, and Jack was probably scared of Kevin and most definitely scared to be stuck in a dough man. (Its also known that Jack's parents didn't know what to do after they found out what their son turned into, and before Jack could really understand the situation, he began panicking and accidentally killed his parents, which probably played more into the thought that Jack's sadness and grief were enough to dim Matthew's protective state, and its also why Doey's final form has 3 faces and how the last time we saw Matthew's side was when he was apologizing to 'Playler,' probably after Kevin's anger calmed down and Jack faded away.).

TO SUM IT UP DOEY IS BIG BIPOLAR

Content:
The people who keep commenting about Poppy's "betrayal" are REALLY starting to tick me off. Cory didn't read them in this video, but go google Riley's notes from this chapter. 

The orphaned kids who were brought to Playcare with the promise of a safe place to call home were instead dragged away in the night to be used as experiments to create living toys. These experiments involved completely being cut up and mutilated to the point where they were barely alive, then their body parts being shoved inside toys. They were then locked up, tortured and isolated for years in the prison, even being mocked by the guards. We can see from her tape talking to "Ollie", who she trusted and confided in with EVERYTHING, that Poppy got some of the worst of this treatment. If you know anything about psychology and childhood trauma, calling her running away at the end of this chapter a "betrayal" is so juvenile and shallow minded! Yes it's a game lol but it annoys me when people don't understand things like this and start talking nonsense like, "she just abandoned us and turned her back on us, the doctor was right she only cares about herself" BRO. She is a terrified traumatised child who's been tortured for years and ran away in a moment of fear and panic. Her plan to finally be free from her suffering (and hello??? She wanted to save the orphans how is that only caring about herself) was ruined after finding out her friend was the Prototype all along- a creature who was working alongside Doctor Sawyer, the man who was responsible for ALL her suffering. PEOPLE!!!! Come on.

Content:
My thoughts are that Elliot Ludwig is Prototype, and that Elliot/Prototype was posing as Ollie to gain poppy's trust even before the hour of joy, because something like the Hour of Joy would need months or even a few years to plan. I also think that it was always Ollie/Elliot, because Ollie was talking to Poppy at 1:09:48 through a phone, so he never gets an actual introduction where hes isn't communicating via walkie talkie or telephone of some type.

One theory that brought me to think that it was Elliot, was because of the tape in Chapter 2. His face was blurred out, and it cut off during a certain part. And we all know that Elliot LOVED kids, and as we also know, The Prototype took all of the orphans to the lab, instead of letting them be eaten in the Hour of Joy. 

In Chapter 3, Ollie was introduced as a child. But, we later find out that Ollie was talking to Poppy before the Hour of Joy, which was 10 or so years ago. This factor wouldn't make sense, because Ollie sounds to be around 8 or 10 years old, so why would he still be a child even after the Hour of Joy? As we know, The Pototype can mimic voices, as I did for Ollie's at the end of Chapter 4. So, the real Ollie could be in the lab, and we might get to meet him during Chapter 5. He also might be an adult, since he was a child before the Hour of Joy, and it's been 10 or so years. 

The factory shut down during the early 2000's after the Hour of Joy, and then the player comes back 10 years later, so this takes place in at least the early 2010's because of a book easter egg. The book that was hidden on one of the shelves is a real book that was released in 2002, meaning that the Hour of Joy had happened between 2003 and 2004, which places out return timeline in 2013 to 2014.

Author: @sp1ritu4l65
Content:
Honestly, I can't entirely blame Poppy for her actions. Being locked up in a box for as long as she was had to be horrifying and deeply traumatic, especially for a child like her who may not fully understand the morality behind her actions, both now and in the past. ON TOP OF THIS, she was even betrayed by a supposed "friend" she was talking to for YEARS, just for it to be "The Prototype" all along, but let's be real, we all saw this coming with how egotistical this persona named "Ollie" actually was, especially for a "child."

By now, it's blatantly obvious that the corporation doesn’t have good intentions, either for the characters or for the community it targets (most likely civilization). Whatever "The Prototype" is after, it's definitely taking its time… assembling something.

What I’ve noticed, though, is that while all the "toys," even the corrupted ones, seem unhinged, crazy, monstrous, and yet we still don’t fully understand what actually corrupted them. What changed them? What made them hungry for blood? Were Huggy, Momma Long Legs, CatNap, The Smiling Critters, Boxxy, Yarnaby, The Delightful Sisters, and all the others always sadistic killers? Though some of them have feelings, free will, and identities related to their lives both inside and/or outside the facility. Onn the outside, appearing to be as if they are joyful playful toys putting on the idea of friendliness, but on the inside, they are something else entirely.

Huggy, Momma, CatNap, and the other toys appear to have organic components within them. Because of this, I can't fully understand how they could be considered ‘automatons,’ as they would require a set directive and a main power source. In contrast, if they were made to merely fit the design of prosthetic-like products: toys, yet how would they feel hunger? They would need cells, organs, and other biological necessities to function.

'The Hour of Joy,' mentioned throughout the story, seems like a major turning point for the entire corporation. However, I could be wrong—perhaps they were all simply created this way and forced to wait... to act. Maybe the entire event was a trap, a spectacle delusion designed to lure people in with ads and attractions before the trap was finally sprung. But for what purpose?

I’m honestly shocked that people outside the facility haven’t questioned how so many individuals have disappeared, or why no more toys are being produced for the public. Perhaps, by the time the main story takes place, they all already know—and realize there’s nothing they can do.

Ignorance is definitely bliss. I just see so many plot holes, I crave an explanation the story now honestly. Chapter 5 better be good.

Author: @chiemirs
Content:
this game feels like it represents so many kinds of childhood trauma that kids experience and deal with later in life. you have to take the story in a way thats deeper than face value to really understand. for example, doey seems to represent bipolar disorder or maybe borderline personality disorder, caused by neglect and parentification. poppy could have abandonment disorder, causing her to self sabotage and neglect others out of fear of being trapped/abandoned again. 

i watched a video by the game theorists that broke down the storyline with some fan theories and info from the games / books, they said poppy was the first toy to come alive. elliot had an adopted daughter who ended up passing away. i don't remember the cause but it isnt that important i think(?). elliot had some of her body (maybe brain? something of the sort) put into a poppy doll which brought her to life. elliot saw that and wanted to bring more toys to life like her, so he brought in sawyer who was a former member of playtime's "young geniuses program" that was originally kicked out for having no humanity. of course, i won't spoil the whole video in case someone wants to watch it, but it was really well put together and very thorough about the storyline! 

i would love if this was a game with a deeper meaning about childhood trauma. it's really important to have representation in media and i'm so appreciative of it, even if it wasn't really the devs intentions.

Author: @redhaired0001
Content:
I believe Eliot Ludwig is Experiment 1006 (The Prototype), and here’s why. The Prototype is far more intelligent than the other failed experiments, almost as if it were someone who already had knowledge of the factory and its operations. If Eliot Ludwig somehow became The Prototype, this would explain its ability to control other toys and manipulate the events happening in Playtime Co.

There’s also the theory that Poppy is actually his daughter, whom he turned into a doll to preserve her in some way. If this is true, it explains why she is so different from the other toys (ability to speak, knowledge). That being said, if they were truly enemies, why didn’t The Prototype kill Poppy while she was still locked inside the case in Chapter 1? It could mean that, at first, she wasn’t a threat to him—but the moment she started helping the player, things changed.

This could also connect to the eerie whisper of “Come back home” in the Chapter 4 ending. If Eliot is still in there somewhere, perhaps he’s calling Poppy back. The biggest mystery is Eliot Ludwig’s unknown fate. The game never confirms what happened to him, and given how obsessed he was with his experiments, it’s possible he took things too far and became 1006 himself.

I also feel like Poppy is hiding something dark. While she appears to help the player, there are moments where she seems manipulative, like when she suddenly locks the train in Chapter 2. What if she isn’t as innocent as she seems? Maybe she has her own plans that we haven’t fully uncovered yet. If this theory turns out to be true, it would completely change how we see the story of Poppy Playtime. What do you think? Could Eliot Ludwig really be The Prototype, and is Poppy truly on our side?

Author: @rosealicia1782
Content:
1:24:26 I like that the whole running thing with Yarnaby is literally just him leisurely walking after you while we're just sprinting for our lives.

Edit: While I'm here. I may as well state that while the sheep later on seems OP and needs to be nerfed a bit, Yarnaby was absolutely toned down as far as movement goes. Given he is modeled after a lion, if Yarnaby has the same physical prowess and speed a real lion did in the game we'd be cooked. For reference. A lion's top speed is 50mph. It can leap (horizontally) 36-40 feet (smaller end of average length of a humpback whale) and 12-18ft (vertically) Not to mention lions are roughly anywhere from 160-240 pounds across the board. So to have a hunter that weighs that much being able to cross almost 330ft in *four seconds* is terrifying. It would have made the game so much harder with that alone, paired with how lions hunt.

During a hunt, lions use their speed effectively by coordinating with their pride. One or two lions will sneak up on the prey, and then they will use their explosive speed to pounce before the prey can react. This strategy makes the most of their ability to sprint fast over short distances.

So lucky Yarnaby is solo here and toned down significantly.

spoilers

this chapter was absolutely insane, for sure my favorite out of all the chapters. i totally agree with you on your points regarding chapter 3, it definitely felt like there was more puzzles than anything and due to that my hype was only centered around the cliffhanger ending. for chapter 4, however, it wasn’t like that at all it really seems like the devs listened to the complaints people had about chapter 3 and kept it in mind while making this chapter, this definitely helps me see poppy playtime in a much better light. to add on the lore, the plot twists, all of that made my jaw drop. it’s insane how we technically didn’t even meet ollie, it was just the prototype using their voice. i thought the ollie we were speaking to was a good/real person because they helped us throughout the entirety of chapter 3, but now thinking back to that chapter the amount of information ollie had was unusual and makes sense for it to be the prototype. then poppy betraying us?? i thought she was a real one it’s unfortunate that the only true person we have is kissy missy, the doctor really was right about her. but overall, i can’t wait for the next chapter, hopefully i’m alive next year and hopefully you are too as i rather not watch anyone else but you play this game, call it glaze but watching you play poppy playtime will never not be entertaining.

Content:
*quick spoiler/theory*

Cory you missed a really cool bonus tape during the chase scene with Doey!! it actually touches on a really popular theory about Poppy. basically its a red tape, you have to grab it quickly as you're running before the rocks fall on it. if you manage to grab it, it basically talks about poppy's experience and whatnot. but she also mentions an interesting detail, she mentioned her dad having something to do with all this. I believe Poppy is Elliot Ludwigs daughter. I remember Cory asking why Poppy was the main character in this story, if Poppy truly is Elliot's daughter then that would make sense as to why she's the one of the main characters even though she hasnt had too many appearances, (and why the game is named after her). There's also another theory that the prototype is Elliot Ludwig himself but i'm not too sure on that, although there are tiny hints that would touch on that. For example, in the 2nd chapter we see Poppy's "bedroom" is right outside of Elliot's office. And the prototype keeps telling her to "come home" and keep her in her box forever. if i remember correctly, Elliot's daughter had a condition and was dying. So he couldve put her into that doll and tried to keep her locked in her room for eternity, to try and protect her. Notice how the prototype never mentioned killing her whatsoever? Just putting her back inside her box? meanwhile he couldnt care less about Kissy or us (mc) dying. If Elliot truly is the Prototype, it could make sense as to why Poppy is being so overshadowed and protected. What COULD be the Prototype's objective is to lure us down by manipulating Poppy into thinking that there are orphans that need to be saved (there end up being no orphans there and we get tricked again by him) ultimately having her bring us to him. Then he'll lock poppy up (likely to protect her), and use one of the monsters to beat us up a bit and bring us to him. Then he'll take our body and use it to escape the factory with his daughter. (just a speculation again guys nothing is confirmed)


(i have another theory bare with me)

I also believe the character we're playing as may have had something to do with the children who were being experimented on, we were most likely one of the high level scientists or something of the sort.  
In the part with the red smoke, if you stand there too without moving your character will start to hear voices and noises. I forgot what the voice lines were i'd have to go back to listen again.... but I do remember that one of the noises was a faint nature sound, the same exact noise you hear when you go downstairs into that room at the end (the room where you play the last vhs tape). Since the red smoke is supposed to make you go to sleep, these hallucinations are very likely coming from the main character's mind. Like having flashbacks before passing out. If so, we were most likely having flashbacks to our days working down there and hearing that nature sound, likely couldve been played while they were on shift to relax their minds from all the horrors going on.

Content:
So here the details on the videos you either missed or weren't able to watch.


Warning Spoilers:






The Warden and the Doctor - An incident with the Prototype acting up and some of the subjects lurking which frighten the Warden and intrigued the Doctor hence foreshadowed the partnership between the Doctor and Prototype. The Doctor, who's body is now in the machine, recommends Warden to give him the Omni-Hand in order to keep him "safe" during procedures and ensure none of the experiments, especially the Prototype, escape. Warden gives him the hand in order for the Doctor to help him get to safety which obviously the Doctor has no intention to help at all.

Leith, Eddie and Stella - A discussion between Eddie Pierre, Eddie Ritterman and Stella Greyber on what to do with the Doctor as he going rogue and doing whatever he wants with the experiments which is costing casualties and delaying further projects. Getting rid of him was out of the question as his genius was needed. So this will led up to the Doctor's brain transferred and to a computer that only those with authorization can control.

Jackie's Parents - Confirmation that Doey IS Jackie who was the child that fell into the dough at the start of the chapter. The video depicts his parents being able to see Doey/Jackie yet he is completely unstable due to the procedure and devoured both of his parents at a fit of rage and hunger. 


Untitled Tape - Poppy confirming that she was aware about the Hour of Joy yet she assumed they were just gonna escape, not commit an entire massacre and the Prototype doesn't want no one to leave ever. She shares her deep hatred of the Prototype, the factory and the fact that the Prototype is right in a sense that they can't leave to ensure history doesn't repeat itself (though there might be an ulterior motive on the Prototype's part). She is disgusted on how the toys have to eat the remains to survive yet knows they will starve. The end of the video confirms that Poppy is Elliot Ludwig's daughter as she mourns and misses him.

Content:
I wholeheartedly believe that all three 'doe boys' were used in creating Doey and not just one of them. I may end up being wrong, but that's really what it seems like.

For one, Doey arguing with himself. He was switching between aggression and then trying to pull himself back, to remain rational. While, of course, any other single-child toy could do smth similar, I just feel like, based off how the subjects were described, it makes sense that he was arguing with himself that way, especially verbally.

ANOTHER THING, when Doey switches into his 'boss mode' the the bot-looking things in his mouth. There looks to be three of them, or at least three heads. What else was there three of? The 'doe boys.' So, I feel like that could also tie into that.

And in general with how each boy was described. Kevin was described to be violent and aggressive, even with friends, while Matthew and Jack were known to be more docile and nice. So, of course, with clashing personalities and character traits in one body, Doey's mannerisms and behaviour makes a lot of sense.

All-in-all, at the end of the day, they were all still kids. And, clearly (from my perception anyway), all three were stressed, upset, and overwhelmed with the situation. And to that, I say: "Same, Doey, same." Bc this chapter was an emotional rollercoaster. Wtf.

Content:
Poppy: (crying)

Ollie: Poppy?...Are you there?

Ollie: Something's bothering you Poppy. Something you... need to talk about?

Poppy: I don"t need anything tonight. Ollie, I just want to sleep. 

Ollie: I think there's more to this. More that you're not telling me.

Poppy: There's not.

Ollie: I know what you're doing Poppy.Talking like that. Don't think for a second that I believe it. Just tell me what you're feeling. Please just talk to me honestly.

Poppy: Talk? Talk?! You want me to talk!?

Ollie: Yes, yes I-

Poppy: And what will talking do, huh!? Will talking to you make them stop?! 

Ollie: N-No it-

Poppy: I'm scared, Ollie. Is that what you want to hear? I'm scared, and I'm angry and-... And I really don't know what to do... The bad men don't say what they want. They don't listen. They don't care how much anything hurts... It's been weeks and weeks of taking things out and putting them back in and taking things 
out and putting them back in. Over and over and over. Nothing's EVER gotten better. And it'll never GET better. But you know what scares me more than anything, Ollie? It scares me that evertime they do it... Everytime they peel me open... I feel it less! LESS !... I hate them... And I hate him... and i hate.... I'm nothing now, Ollie. No one. I'm a thing... And nothing that they do hurts me more than that...

Ollie: You're not nothing to me. You're Poppy. And talking with you. Like this... I know it doesn't make any of what they do right. It can't... It makes me feel like a piece of me is still here. No matter how small they try make it. Next to all that. Next to everything they do... it means everything.

Poppy: (crying)

Ollie: I'm here Poppy. For you. I'll always be here...

Doey has been such a great supporting character with lots of physical strength too (I mean, he easily took down Pianosaurus). Content:
Cory for the difference, during the tests and experiments some of the toys were just messed with. They were attempting to recreate The Prototype and Poppy which resulted in the tests, but some of the people and kids used just weren't compatible with the toys which resulted in them becoming animalistic and primal. The difference between Kissy Missy, Poppy, Catnap, and The Prototype all lie in their compatibility with what there put in and also if it was willing. Catnap was willingly put inside the toy body and he was compatible with it so he retained his cognitive function and rationality, he just chose to work for the Protoype.
Poppy was willing to be turned into Poppy and was compatible, same with Kissy Missy, so they retained rationality and sanity.
Huggy Wuggy was NOT willing nor compatible with the toy he was put inside, so he became violent and like an animal, The Protoype sort of tamed Huggy.
Basically the difference between Rational and Animalistic toys is whether they wanted to be turned into that specific toy or not.

Content:
Consider things from Poppy's perspective.
The toys are abominations, for lack of a better term. They really shouldn't exist and while pushing the bounds of science, their creation was morally corrupt. If they leave the factory, into the world, there is no guarantee that another, Harley Sawyer won't find them and try to create more monsters just like them. Blowing up the factory may just be the best means to bury everything so history does not repeat itself.

About her abandoning us: Poppy was locked inside a case for approximately 10 whole years. She knows that if the Prototype finds her, he'll put her back, or worse. She may not have wanted to, but running away was likely her best chance of surviving.

I don't agree with her methods, but I can understand her reasons.

Content:
Hey Cory!! If you read this comment then Im a HUGE fan of your horror gaming series and I would love to inform you on all the specifics of the scenes in this video.

Safe Haven Blowing Up: You were right when Poppy led Doey out so he can be out the way. But that was because Poppy may or may not have made a deal with The Prototype, sacrificing her friends in Safe Haven in return for freedom to not be in the box anymore (As we saw in the end of Chapter 1). This confirms that The Prototype intentionally lost Doey in the mines so it can gather the charged bombs and plant them in daycare. Why else do you think the small dolls were in the foundation leading you away?

Doey's creation: Matthew, Kevin, and Samuel are all separate kids who were killed in the dough that made Doey. People theorize that if it wasnt for Kevin (the 'problem child') for getting in the dough, then we would've never had a boss fight. But because scientists found out his body was perfect for the tests, they kept him inside.

The Red Smoke: We may figure out how it was made in Chapter 3 or 5, but many people believe the smoke is either from CatNap's breath, or Poppy's poppyflower  scent, hence was all the poppies were in the last part of the game. Maybe the Prototype needs Poppy because he can make more of the gas that keeps the children asleep and "fresh".

CatNap and the Prototype: We just find out about this in Chapter 4. The Prototype only needed CatNap for the children that was in Playcare. But after he got them, he had no need for CatNap, hence why he murdered him.

Author: @CuteAs-a-Mango
Content:
So I just got finished with watching this chapter and holy crap.. I am absolutely speechless. With how puzzle-driven chapter 3 was, my expectations for this one was pretty low, but chapter 4 didn’t even exceed my expectations, it blew them out of the water.

*SPOILER WARNING AHEAD*

There’s a lot to unpack here.
First of all, the voice-acting, writing, and storytelling for this chapter was PHE👏NO👏ME👏NAL.
The whole therapeutic talk between Ollie and Poppy genuinely made me emotional with “a piece of Ollie” always being with him no matter how much the employees of Playtime Co. try to distort it. And it also felt really disturbing to hear Poppy barely hold back her cries and screams as she describes “being peeled apart” over and over from testing.
Nowhere in the voice acting did it feel stiff, wooden, or ingenuine. 
I also don’t know if it’s just me, but I noticed that Ollie in chapter 3 seemed to be a lot calmer and almost robotic-sounding while this Ollie seemed to show a lot more emotion and emphasis in their wording. Could that mean the Prototype was getting better at disguising themselves compared to the beginning at chapter 3 and the end of chapter 4? Dunno.
The whole sequence of Doey’s crashout and the three different children switching in and out was really well done by the voice actor, and felt sadder knowing each of the souls were just kids that wanted a home and people to care about them. Jack crying out for his parents, Matthew beating himself up for not being able to save the toys in Safe Haven, and then Kevin seeming to be the main controller of the anger-driven monster Doey becomes.

1:25:37 One of my other favorite parts of this chapter is that we get to hear a recording of one of the Smiling Critter’s voices before they were all annihilated by Catnap, Hoppy! Although it’s probably not gonna happen anytime soon, it’d be really cool if one of the other 7 Smiling Critters make a callback through a secret tape of some kind.

I appreciate Kissy Missy getting more screentime than the last 2 chapters and how much of her personality was fleshed out. It’s impressive how despite her never saying a single word, the most itty bitty details of her actions speak volumes. She helped the player in the second chapter, she’s always letting Poppy ride her shoulder and reach things she can’t, and even when all hope was lost she still tried to catch the player from falling any deeper into the hell Poppy dragged him into. She's kind, compassionate, patient, strong both mentally and physically, and selfless: 2:30:10

As much as I loved Ollie and Poppy’s talk, Doey’s transformation (forgot to mention it but him screaming in pain and using his last breath to mutter, “sorry” right before he dies is heavily heartbreaking: 2:20:16 ), hearing Doey’s voice one last time through the tape recording he made, the Doctor’s bossfight sequence, the introduction to Safe Haven, hearing Hoppy for the first time, Ollie being revealed to be the Prototype.. But this entire sequence right here of what was originally thought to be like every other tape smoothly transition into being a surprise-alarm, and then the next scene showing Huggy Wuggy had been alive this entire time was the most sickest conclusion I’ve seen in this game: 2:31:49 – 2:33:00 (Cory’s reaction was identical to mine lmao)



TLDR: Immaculate improvement from the last chapter, excellent voice-acting, crazy writing, awesome character designs as always, clever twist villians, and I am _HYPED_ to see what Mobgames will cook up for chapter 5.
